**Refined prompt:** Design (not implement) a `Comment.author` relation for this NestJS/TypeORM RealWorld API — schema change, write path, read path, response shape, and the ownership check it unblocks — answering as a maintainer bound by `LESSONS.md`, the RO-envelope/nested-body/layer-order conventions, `synchronize: true` with no migrations, and spec conformance as the contract; delivered as a phased design with file:line citations and explicit open decisions.

---

# Design: `comment.author`

## Why it's missing and what it blocks

`Comment` has exactly three fields — `id`, `body`, `article` (`src/article/comment.entity.ts:5-15`). Two things depend on the gap:

1. The spec's comment object has an `author` profile; we can't produce it (`schema.md:50-58`).
2. `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:10-12` — the 403 on `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id` has nothing to compare the caller against (`article.service.ts:114-129` never sees a user id).

---

## Phase 1 — The relation

```ts
// comment.entity.ts
@ManyToOne(type => UserEntity, { eager: true, onDelete: 'SET NULL' })
author: UserEntity;
```

**Three decisions inside that one line:**

**`eager: true`** — recommended, and the tradeoff is real. `LESSONS.md:68-76` ("a relation that is not eager is `undefined`, not `[]`") is exactly the trap waiting here: the ownership check in Phase 3 reads `comment.author.id` off `this.commentRepository.findOne(id)` (`article.service.ts:117`), which honours eager relations but returns `author === undefined` without them. Eager also nests correctly under the already-eager `ArticleEntity.comments` (`article.entity.ts:40`), so `findOne`/`findComments` get authors for free. The cost is that the raw `UserEntity` — **including the argon2 hash** — rides along in every article load, which Phase 2 has to contain.

The surgical alternative is non-eager plus explicit `relations: ['author']` at the two call sites. It leaks less by default but relies on every future caller remembering. Given that `LESSONS.md` already records this class of bug twice, I'd take eager + a hard boundary mapper.

*Scope note:* `findAll()` builds articles through a QueryBuilder (`article.service.ts:28-30`), which does not apply eager relations — so article **list** responses carry no comments today and won't after this change. Only the `articleRepository.findOne` paths are affected.

**Nullable** — `@ManyToOne` is nullable by default, and that's required, not incidental. There are no migration files; tables come from the entities at boot (`workspace.md:22`). A `NOT NULL` FK added to a `comment` table with existing rows fails or silently backfills garbage. Pre-existing comments stay `author IS NULL`, so **every consumer must handle a null author** — Phase 2 maps it to a placeholder, Phase 3 treats it as "not yours" (403).

**`onDelete: 'SET NULL'`** — `DELETE /users/:slug` is public and unauthenticated (`auth.md:48`). Without an explicit rule, deleting a user with comments hits an FK constraint or orphans rows. `SET NULL` keeps the thread intact and reuses the null-author path we already need.

**Not adding** the `@OneToMany` inverse on `UserEntity` (alongside `articles` at `user.entity.ts:37-38`). Nothing reads "all comments by user," and an unused non-eager relation is one more `undefined` waiting to be dereferenced.

---

## Phase 2 — Populating and returning it

### Write path

The route is already guarded (`article.module.ts:28`), so `req.user` is set — the controller just isn't asking for it. Mirror `create()` (`article.controller.ts:52`):

```ts
@Post(':slug/comments')
async createComment(@User('id') userId: number, @Param('slug') slug,
                    @Body('comment') commentData: CreateCommentDto)
```

…threading `userId` into `addComment()` (`article.service.ts:101`), which looks the user up and assigns `comment.author` before `save`.

**`CreateCommentDto` stays `{ body }`** (`dto/create-comment.ts:1-3`). The author comes from the token, never the body — `LESSONS.md:39-47` is precisely the case where an `authorId` in the request body gets persisted because the DTO is a type annotation, not a runtime filter. `addComment` assigns field-by-field today; keep it that way.

### Read path — the boundary mapper

This is the part that isn't optional. `CommentsRO`'s element type is `{ body: string }` (`article.interface.ts:3-5`) while `findComments()` returns live `Comment` entities (`article.service.ts:167`) — the interface is already a fiction. With an eager author it becomes a password-hash leak.

Add to `article.interface.ts`:

```ts
export interface CommentData {
  id: number;
  body: string;
  author: ProfileData;   // from profile/profile.interface.ts:1-6
}
export interface CommentsRO { comments: CommentData[]; }
export interface CommentRO  { comment: CommentData; }
```

…and a private `ArticleService.buildComment()` that **constructs** the profile field-by-field, the way `ProfileService.findProfile()` does (`profile.service.ts:35-39`) — *not* `delete user.password` on a loaded entity the way `findOne()` does (`profile.service.ts:26`), which mutates a managed object that some later `save` could write back.

Null author → `{ username: '[deleted]', bio: '', image: '', following: false }` rather than `null`, so clients that render `comment.author.username` unconditionally don't break.

### `author.following`

The spec's comment author carries `following`, which needs the caller's identity on a **public** route (`article.controller.ts:43-46`, absent from `article.module.ts:24-31`). Add `@User('id') userId` — the decorator returns `undefined` when no token is sent (`user.decorator.ts:13-17`), which is the intended behaviour here.

No cross-module service call needed: `ArticleService` already holds `followsRepository` (`article.service.ts:23`, injected at `article.module.ts:13`). Query it **once per request** — `find({ followerId: userId })` → `Set` of `followingId`, same shape as `findFeed()` (`article.service.ts:67`) — rather than per comment, or a 20-comment thread becomes 20 queries.

Two known hazards on that route: `@User()` will 500 on an expired token because nothing catches `jwt.verify` (`LESSONS.md:29-37`, `user.decorator.ts:15`) — pre-existing, but this change puts a public endpoint behind it for the first time. And `findProfile` only sets `following` when `id` is truthy (`profile.service.ts:43-44`), leaving it absent for anonymous callers; the spec wants `false`. I'd emit `false` and flag the divergence rather than mirror the sibling's omission.

---

## Phase 3 — What this unblocks (the 403)

With `comment.author` loaded eagerly, `deleteComment` (`article.service.ts:114-129`) gains the comparison `LESSONS.md:18-27` demands you be able to point at:

```ts
if (!comment.author || comment.author.id !== userId) {
  throw new HttpException('You are not the author.', HttpStatus.FORBIDDEN);
}
```

…with `userId` threaded from `@User('id')` in the controller (`article.controller.ts:84-88`, currently takes only `@Param()`). This is the line that makes the existing `@ApiResponse({ status: 403 })` at `article.controller.ts:83` true instead of aspirational.

Per the RealWorld spec, the article author may also delete comments on their own article — that's a second `||` clause, but note `articleRepository.findOne({slug})` (`article.service.ts:115`) does **not** load `article.author` (non-eager, `schema.md:42`), so it needs an explicit `relations: ['author']` or it's the undefined-relation bug again.

---

## Deliberately out of scope — flagging, not fixing

- **`POST /articles/:slug/comments` returns `{article}`, not `{comment}`** (`article.service.ts:111`). The spec returns the created comment. This is `LESSONS.md:49-57` (#57) in waiting — but changing it is a breaking response change, separable from adding the relation. `CommentRO` above is defined so it's a one-line follow-up.
- **`Comment` has no `createdAt`/`updatedAt`** — spec requires both. Same `@Column({type:'timestamp'})` + `@BeforeUpdate()` pattern as `article.entity.ts:23-32`. Belongs with the timestamp-renaming work already in `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:7-9`.
- **`ArticleRO` is typed as the raw `ArticleEntity`** (`article.interface.ts:24-26`), and `findAll()` joins the author in (`article.service.ts:30`) — so **article list responses already expose author password hashes today.** Independent of this change, but the same root cause, and worth its own item.

---

**Read for this:** `comment.entity.ts`, `article.entity.ts`, `article.service.ts`, `article.controller.ts`, `article.module.ts`, `article.interface.ts`, `dto/create-comment.ts`, `user.entity.ts`, `user.decorator.ts`, `profile.service.ts`, `profile.interface.ts`, plus the KB (`workspace.md`, `schema.md`, `auth.md`), `LESSONS.md`, `CURRENT_FOCUS.md`.

**Not read:** `user.service.ts`, `auth.middleware.ts` (relied on `auth.md`), `user.interface.ts`, `shared/pipes/validation.pipe.ts`, `main.ts`, `app.module.ts`, `tag/`, and `prisma/` (excluded as a parallel experiment per `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:21-24`). Nothing was written — this is design only.

The open decision I'd want your call on before implementing: **does the article's author also get to delete comments on their article** (spec says yes, costs an extra relation load), and **do the POST-response and timestamp fixes ship with this or separately**?
